dimensions.abu-saraj-iv17: Plan 5 scale, 3 m / 178 sampled pixels. Uniform height 1.55 m within reported 1.4–1.7 m. Roof cap, rock thickness, masonry height and scan sampling illustrative.
dimensions.hyrcania-waterworks: Northern pool floor at -5 m, southern member at -2.6 m; approximate published northern sides. Rock separation 5.1 m within reported 4.8–5.4 m. Southern footprint, bridge, summit and other cistern dimensions illustrative.
dimensions.gerizim-precinct: Reported 212 × 136 m enclosure, 40 × 40 m mansion, 20 × 14 m building IV, 25 × 24 m citadel. East stair uses maximum 23 m width, 34 m run, 15.5 m rise and approximately 57 steps. Western landing distinct from southern seven-step and E1 flights. Other heights, divisions, cistern and platform relief illustrative.
dimensions.jericho-early: Approximate 18 × 13 m pool envelopes; 2.5 m depth, columns and platform illustrative.
dimensions.jericho-late: Approximate 32 × 18 m joined envelope; 2.5 m depth, columns and platform illustrative.
dimensions.relative_models: Doq, Qumran, Siloam and Area AC are normalized relative frames. Heights/depths and channel cross-sections illustrative; selection envelopes are not measured footprints.

landscape.method: Modern elevation sampled around existing site anchors, with a feathered display bench and source-qualified architectural volumes. Terrain is contextual; footprint placement and compass bearing are illustrative. IV/17 uses an illustrative setting without coordinates.

surface_art.method: Original deterministic 512-pixel colour and relief/roughness tiles, projected in world metres. Separate masonry, limestone, stratified bedrock, soil and plaster treatments. Physical chipped stone courses, coping, open channel troughs, grounded rubble and sparse vegetation; no publication or photograph pixels are used as texture maps. Dominant-axis projection preserves hard surface detail; soil combines two differently oriented samples to reduce visible tiling.

profiles.Qumran: Warm fractured limestone and dusty ground; uneven crest, tapering rock beds, short weathered ledges and an angular recess. An irregular feathered ground apron replaces the rectangular tile.
profiles.Doq: Ochre limestone and rough desert masonry around the plan-derived cistern/channel relations.
profiles.Hyrcania: Cream limestone and muted plaster distinguish the paired basins.
profiles.Jericho: Warm stone, reddish soil and pale worn plaster; source states remain separate.
profiles.Gerizim: Cooler ashlar palette and sparse sage vegetation around the precinct/stair relationships.
profiles.Siloam: Grey-gold limestone and muted plaster around the small receiving-basin tracing.

surface_art.evidence_limit: Palette, chipping, individual stone joints, cliff bedding, plaster wear, rubble, vegetation, light and sky are illustrative surface art. These additions supply no new archaeological observations, dimensions, phase assignments or identification evidence.
surface_art.rendering: Directional sun, hemisphere fill, ACES tone mapping, static shadow map, eye-level sky; 2048-pixel desktop / 1024-pixel phone shadow atlas. Repeated masonry and scree use GPU instancing. Thin soil floors receive shadows without casting self-shadow artifacts. Regional source layers pause at eye level and regain their individual visibility on exit; the site and sky continue rendering in the same geographic canvas.
surface_art.camera: Initial eye-level positions frame a source feature such as the eastern stair, pool rim or channel. These are display viewpoints, not surveyed camera positions or walking routes. Eye-level look can pass above the horizon to inspect cliff faces and tall structures; exiting restores the normal geographic camera limits. The first-person camera now follows a physical capsule body, with gravity and clearance against the displayed geometry; the 70-degree world view has one camera-relative blocky right forearm in its lower-right corner.
surface_art.covered_passages: The normalized Reeder–Jol scene uses angular rock-cut display sections in place of smooth tubes. Their rectangular roof section is illustrative. A copper-coloured lining retains the proposed-course distinction in the source.

unified_map.renderer: MapLibre shared geographic WebGL canvas with a Three.js custom layer. Source-based 3D appears on close zoom; eye-level inspection uses the same camera and canvas.
unified_map.placement: Existing site anchors only. Architectural bearing, local origin, relative display scale and alignment remain illustrative; this interface does not register the source plans to the earth.
unified_map.qumran: Detailed aqueduct segment reuses the existing Ilan–Amit 1989 p. 283 Fig. 1 relationships and existing Davey CJD979 comparison. Rock faces, masonry weathering, cross-sections and heights are illustrative; the whole settlement is not reconstructed.
unified_map.walking: Embodied first-person character: 1.8 m high, 0.30 m capsule radius, standing eye 1.62 m, crouching height 1.5 m and eye 1.27 m. Minecraft Java-style impulses, friction and gravity run at 20 Hz with collision and position updates at 120 Hz. Ground, rock, walls and ceilings collide; 0.60 m steps, a 50-degree slope limit, head clearance and sneaking at unsupported ledges are enforced. Repeated masonry uses oriented bounding boxes; small pebbles and vegetation are excluded. Qumran collision geometry rebuilds after loaded map terrain deforms it. The single camera-relative right forearm stays in the lower-right corner. Walking reaches 4.317 m/s, sprinting 5.612 m/s and sneaking 1.295 m/s; jumping rises about 1.25 m. Sprint-jumping adds directional momentum and held jump repeats after landing. These display/collision approximations do not establish a surveyed ancient route.
unified_map.photos: Original licensed source JPEGs are archived with provenance at research/assets/plans/atlas-ground-photographs; matching atlas mirror and public copies retain identical bytes, authors and license links.
unified_map.videos: The two existing Qumran YouTube leads are labeled unreviewed. They are inline reference players, not inspected geometry input or registered camera tracks. User-entered links store video IDs locally in the browser.
unified_map.access: No fresh private Google Drive file retrieval or live YouTube playback verification is claimed. Inline Drive preview uses the viewer account permissions; provider domains are saved in the environment draft.
unified_map.validation: The full map regression used the exact actions/jekyll-build-pages image to generate an 88.8 MiB site. Every app file retains its source bytes, startup assets resolve and the research archives are excluded. Chromium checks against that actual Pages output passed on desktop and phone: rendered source geometry, persistent map canvas, inline plan/photo/Drive/video references, eye-level movement, looking above the horizon, return to map, site switching and unavailable-provider messages. A controlled Terrarium DEM at -183 metres verifies that loaded elevation and the rendered model stay in view through Terrain/Map switching. Desktop and phone renders using the existing archived Wadi Qumran Mapterhorn patch were inspected in overview and at eye level: no rectangular soil tile or transparent cut-out edges; soil, rock, scree and channels follow the same slope. The shared ground fix was also inspected at Jericho. Geometry checks verify slope-following stones and channel floors, unchanged horizontal positions, finite geometry, a tapering uneven crest and bounded elevation sampling. Terrain fit, geological form, vertical geometry and map alignment remain illustrative. Live provider coverage, private Drive playback and hardware frame rates are separate from these local checks.

terrain_integration.method: The whole model follows a bounded 9 by 9 grid of loaded map elevations, preserving source-plan horizontal relationships. Soil, rock and instanced scree share the same displacement, and long channel floors follow its local slope. The irregular apron and soil-covered ridge back fade into the map. The crest is uneven and the rock ends taper, replacing the rectangular tile and full-depth slabs. All vertical deformation, terrain fitting and geological scenery are illustrative, not survey registration.
terrain_integration.elevation_loading: Retain last loaded nonzero elevation samples during missing-coverage zero responses, separately from vertical exaggeration. Keep the close-up scale when entering Terrain, and synchronize the camera with loaded elevation while preserving independent eye-level movement.
terrain_integration.regression_fixture: atlas/scripts/fixtures/negative-terrain.png: original constant Terrarium DEM at -183 metres, for a controlled below-sea-level camera and model test; no source-image pixels.
terrain_integration.transparency: Feathered ground and ridge skirts do not write depth, and draw before cliff faces; fully invisible pixels cannot hide ground behind them. The shared landscape ground uses the same rule.

unified_map.character_validation: Measured on level synthetic ground after acceleration: walk 4.317 m/s, sprint 5.612 m/s, sneak 1.295 m/s, diagonal walk 4.317 m/s, jump apex 1.252 m and landing at 0.558 s during the twelfth game tick. Walking and sprint-jump ranges measure 1.880 m and 3.392 m. Held jumps, retained air momentum, quarter-block stopping distance, half-metre steps, sneak ledges, long falls, head clearance, thin/rotated walls, slopes and real Qumran geometry before/after terrain fitting pass. Simulated 30/60/144 Hz rendering preserves travel distance and jump height. Final Chromium checks against actual Pages output (105.2 MiB) pass with normal motion on desktop and reduced motion on phone: all sites and inline references, sustained real masonry collision, tap and held jumping, crouching, W/S sprint controls, phone Sprint/Jump controls, blur clearing movement, wider sprint FOV/return to normal, return to the map, site switching and provider failure handling. These are engine and browser checks, not archaeological measurements or hardware frame-rate benchmarks.

first_person_view.method: One connected cuboid forearm and sleeve, with an original deterministic 16 by 16 skin texture using nearest-neighbour filtering. A separate Three.js camera renders the view model after the world on the existing MapLibre canvas. It stays at the lower-right viewport edge while looking, crouching and moving. The sleeve continues off the viewport; no detached left arm or body meshes are drawn. The view model is separate from the physical collision capsule.
first_person_view.validation: TypeScript and production build pass. Actual actions/jekyll-build-pages output (101.1 MiB) passes byte-for-byte checks for every app file and startup asset. Desktop and phone Chromium renders from that actual output were visually inspected at rest and while looking/crouching: one connected arm enters from the right/bottom edge, with no left arm or floating sleeve edge. Entering, looking, crouching and returning to the map pass without shader/runtime errors.

minecraft_movement.reference_scope: Coefficient comparison of normal, unmodified movement only. The atlas implementation uses its own capsule collision against continuous illustrative site meshes, rather than a voxel world.
minecraft_movement.simulation: 20 Hz horizontal impulses and drag, 0.42 blocks/tick jump impulse, 0.08 blocks/tick^2 gravity, 0.98 vertical drag, 0.546 ground drag, 0.91 air drag, 0.30 sneak input factor, 0.20 blocks/tick directional sprint-jump impulse, 0.50 s held-jump cooldown. Six collision substeps per game tick preserve smooth motion and resolve thin obstacles. A 0.10 s press buffer bridges rendered frames.
minecraft_movement.measurement_scope: Level synthetic ground after acceleration, using foot-position distance. Jump contact is interpolated by collision substeps and lands during the twelfth 20 Hz tick. These engine measurements are not archaeological measurements or hardware frame-rate benchmarks.
minecraft_movement.validation: Numerical speed/diagonal-speed, jump apex/flight/range, repeated held jumps, retained air momentum, stopping distance, half-metre slabs, sneaking at ledges, long-fall landing, ceilings, thin/rotated walls, climbable/steep slopes and Qumran before/after terrain fitting pass. Simulated 30, 60 and 144 Hz rendering preserves walking distance and jump height. Final desktop normal-motion and phone reduced-motion Chromium checks on actual Pages output (105.2 MiB) pass, including a held keyboard/pointer jump through landing and a second takeoff, sustained masonry collision, sprint FOV transition and restoration, crouch, blur and map return.

walking_camera.reproduction: At the existing Qumran anchor with the archived Mapterhorn terrain fixture, replacing MapLibre’s camera terrain sample with its missing-coverage value (zero) changes the camera from approximately -269 m altitude and 86 degrees pitch to sea level and 4.22 degrees pitch. The physical character remains on ground and crouching; its HUD/view model therefore hide the camera displacement. This reproduces the reported tiny-site overhead view.
walking_camera.fix: The physical walking controller supplies the final camera transform using MapLibre’s public transformCameraUpdate hook, after the independent map terrain safety correction. Capsule collision against displayed terrain/architecture remains responsible for walking clearance. The hook is removed on exit. Camera framing also follows viewport and delayed model-base elevation changes. Walking does not overwrite the saved overhead map view.
walking_camera.regression: check-walk-camera-browser.mjs runs the actual controller and MapLibre camera with a controlled -183 m DEM. The old controller fails when the DEM camera sample becomes zero; the fixed controller passes on desktop and phone through crouch, sprint/FOV, jumping, looking, delayed elevation, resize, competing map commands and exit. Actual rendered-frame projection matrices must place the camera within 6 cm of the physical eye, including up to 2.5 cm head bob. check-map-browser.mjs also checks terrain walking and rendered camera alignment during the existing full-app movement checks.
walking_camera.validation: TypeScript, production build and numerical/collision movement checks pass. The previous controller fails the missing-DEM rendered-eye assertion; the fixed controller passes the isolated real-MapLibre camera regression on desktop and phone. Final desktop normal-motion and phone reduced-motion checks against actual actions/jekyll-build-pages output (114.4 MiB) pass: terrain walking/crouch, sustained masonry collision, tap/held jumps, sprint/FOV, looking, inline references, site switching and provider failures. Sampled world-frame projection matrices keep the rendered eye within 6 cm of the physical character. All app files retain their bytes through Jekyll and startup assets resolve. The recorded Mapterhorn/Qumran reproduction was visually checked after the fix; the character remains at eye level during the forced missing sample. These are controlled software-rendered Chromium checks, not a hardware performance benchmark.
